title: LIPOBAR: Effect of bariatric surgery (laparoscopic Roux-Y Gastric-Bypass and laparoscopic Sleeve Gastrectomy) on lipoedema.
summary:
Lipoedema, also known as fat swelling, is a common condition that affects about 11% of women, while it is rare in men and often goes undiagnosed. It is characterized by an abnormal build-up of fat, mostly in the legs, leading to lumpy and fibrous tissue. People with lipoedema often experience swelling, pain, and easy bruising. The exact cause of lipoedema is unknown, but it may be triggered by events like puberty, childbirth, menopause, or stress from incidents like accidents or surgeries. Lipoedema can be divided into five types based on where the fat is distributed and four stages based on the severity.
Treatment depends on how severe the symptoms are and can include: Dietary changes, Weight management, Physical activity, Compression therapy (using special garments to reduce swelling), Pain management, In severe cases, liposuction (surgical fat removal). 

The aim of this study is to see how obesity surgery, such as stomach reduction (sleeve gastrectomy) or gastric bypass, affects lipoedema.

To evaluate these effects, we will conduct several examinations, including:
•	Medical History: Including questionnaires about quality of life.
•	Clinical Examination: To classify the lipoedema.
•	Routine Lab Tests
•	Body Measurements: Using a simple tape measure on different body parts.
•	Bioelectrical Impedance Analysis (BIA): A method to measure body composition.
•	3D Optical Measurement

These assessments will be conducted at different times:
•	Before Surgery: At the initial consultation and after completing a comprehensive treatment plan.
•	After Surgery: At 3, 6, and 12 months post-surgery.

The results from these assessments will be compared to understand how obesity surgery impacts lipoedema.

interventions.name:
Obese patients with lipedema who are undergoing pre- and postoperative preparation for bariatric surgery will receive:
- Medical history (including the occurrence of diabetes mellitus and hypertension as part of metabolic syndrome)
- Questionnaire about Quality of Life (QoL) SF-36
- Physical exam

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-	All patients requiring a bariatric surgery.
-	Patients, with lipoedema, requiring a bariatric surgery (Roux-Y Gastric Bypass or sleeve gastrectomy).
-	Able to understand the nature of the study and what will be required of them.
-	Women (non-pregnant and non-lactating) and men aged 18 years and older.
-	BMI above 35 kg/m2
-	Patients with ASA I-II-III-IV
Exclusion criteria:
-	Inability to give written informed consent.
-	Patients with ASA V.
